competition.summary: MSFT is #2 in cloud infrastructure at 20% share (Synergy, Q2 2026). That share has been flat since Q3 2025 while Google rose from 13% to 15%, and neoclouds (CoreWeave, Oracle, Nebius) plus OpenAI/Anthropic are taking share in a market growing 43%. Productivity is dominant: 30M+ paid M365 Copilot seats (~6.5% of an estimated ~464M commercial seats) and 50M GitHub Copilot users. MSFT holds ~27% of OpenAI, but the Apr 2026 amendment ended IP exclusivity and let OpenAI go multi-cloud.

summary: Microsoft is executing very well: FY26 revenue was $331.8B (+18%), Azure grew 43% last quarter, and commercial RPO jumped 84% to $678B. After rallying from a ~$349 June low to ~$518, the stock trades at ~26x forward EPS, a premium to peers that is justified by ~46% operating margins but leaves little upside against a triangulated fair value of $470-575 (mid $520). Heavy AI capex (~$175B guided) is crushing free cash flow, so a strict FCF DCF looks expensive; the bull case relies on capex turning into earnings. Neutral / hold with a bias to add on pullbacks toward the $470-490 area, and watch the Oct 28 earnings for Azure capacity and capex updates.

valuation.method: Triangulation. (a) Peer multiples: peer median forward P/E 23.3x; MSFT merits a premium for margin and durability, so we apply 24-28x to FY27 consensus EPS of $19.76, giving $474-553. (b) Earnings power: FY27 EPS $19.76 grown 12-14%/yr for 4 years, then a 22-24x exit multiple, discounted at 9% plus dividends, gives ~$460-535. A strict FCF DCF on depressed FY26 FCF ($67B, 15%/8% growth, 8.5% WACC, 3% terminal) gives only ~$340 ($265-455 across scenarios), a reminder of what happens if AI capex never normalises. (c) Analysts: $440 low / $576 average / $870 high (55 analysts). Blended fair range $470-575, mid $520.
valuation.note: Multiples from stockanalysis.com at the Sep 25, 2026 close. The FCF DCF is shown as a bear-case anchor and is not weighted in the range.
